- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model frequently overshoots downward; apply a “lag correction” — delay downward adjustment by 1–2 periods.
- If model shows strong mean reversion bias (e.g., forecasting back to 60s after 70s), check sentiment for support — if sentiment is neutral or positive, allow slight overshoot.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price volatility — add 0.5–1.5% buffer if sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 1.00, 0.00, 1.00), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles — adjust forecast to match sentiment swing direction.
